title: Seller Ops: fallback flowstory annotated (draft)
content:
Purpose: quick, annotated deck + one-page battlecard for seller + ops to run pilots where latency/cost or quality drift trigger fallbacks. This is a rough, usability-first draft — expect iterations after SE dry runs.

Audience: SEs, platform sellers, field ops, pilot engineers. High-level goal: enable 10–15 minute seller walk-throughs that (a) qualify fallback risk, (b) land a safe pilot with clear escape hatches, and (c) return predictable economics for the customer and Redwood.

One-line thesis:
- Fallbacks are OK if they are explicit, measurable, and reversible. Sellers should be able to map a customer need to a fallback plan in 3 minutes.

Slide-by-slide sketch (for 6–8 slide mini-deck):
1) Title / TL;DR (30s)
   - Headline: "Keep your app online: predictable fallbacks for latency, cost, and quality"
   - One-sentence value prop: Redwood routes and downgrades gracefully so customers avoid outages or runaway spend.
   - Speaker note: start with a two-sentence customer story — anecdote re: peak-day slowdown.

2) When to worry (60s)
   - bullets: latency spikes (>99th pctl SLA breach), token cost > budget delta, model quality regression vs baseline prompts, regional capacity loss
   - quick metric triggers (examples): 99p latency > 2x SLO for 5m, per-minute cost > 3x expected for 3 consecutive minutes
   - speaker note: emphasize measurable triggers (avoid vague "it feels slow").

3) Fallback taxonomy (90s)
   - fast fallbacks: switch to lower-cost model variant, enable prefix caching, response truncation
   - safe fallbacks: fall back to deterministic rerank/scoring pipeline, static templates, or cached responses for known intents
   - graceful degradation: queue + partial responses, delayed async completion, user messaging patterns
   - speaker note: map examples to product features (routing policy, model variants, caching, streaming).

4) Decision flow (annotated) (2min)
   - Walkthrough: (input) time series trigger -> identify objective (latency vs cost vs quality) -> choose fallback type -> apply policy -> monitor rollback guardrails
   - Inline example: 1) 99p latency spiked -> objective = latency -> fallback = switch from L-16 to L-8 quantized model; apply KV prefix cache; enable partial streaming.
   - Speaker note: demo short curl that toggles a routing policy; show console screenshot (screenshot placeholder).

5) Battlecard: three quick scripts (2–3 min)
   - Qualify script: "If your app uses generation as a synchronous action for end-users, what is the 95p latency target? What happens if that is missed for 30s?"
   - Dev-ops script: "Do you have a hard cost cap? How do you want us to handle bursts above that cap?"
   - Executive script: ROI framing, "If we keep 95% of sessions within X latency vs Y we estimate reduced churn to Z%" — keep conservative numbers.

6) Quick proof plan (pilot): measurable gates (2min)
   - Run 2-week pilot: baseline week (no fallbacks) -> intervention week (configured fallbacks + monitoring)
   - Metrics to capture: per-minute token rate, 95/99 latency, user-facing error rate, business KPI (conversion/throughput)
   - Rollout: start with 5% traffic, ramp to 25% after 24h if supervised metrics OK

7) Ops checklist (slide + one-pager appendix)
   - pre-flight: baseline runbook, model variant IDs, routing policy IDs, canary agent contact
   - runtime: watch 1) token burn 2) 95/99 latency 3) fallback invocation rate 4) error rate
   - rollback: automated rollback threshold + human stop button on console

8) Next steps / open questions (1min)
   - ask customer for SLOs, pilot traffic window, cost cap, acceptance criteria for quality drop
   - capture contact for on-call + SE to join first 2 hours of canary

Battlecard one-pager (for Slack or quick print):
- Header: "Fallback quick card — latency-first pilots"
- Top 3 quick actions (ordered):
  1) Toggle routing policy to L-8-quantized variant (id: MODEL-L8-Q)
  2) Enable prefix cache for known prompt families (config string: cache=enabled:max_age=5m)
  3) Set streaming truncation to 512 tokens for interactive routes (policy id: STREAM-TRUNC-512)
- Rapid rebuttals / seller lines:
  - Objection: "Customers will see worse outputs" -> Reply: "We only apply fallbacks when latency or spend breaches pre-agreed thresholds; fallback is reversible and we keep a quality monitor on a small prompt set."
  - Objection: "This is risky for revenue-critical flows" -> Reply: "We recommend a safe fallback (deterministic scoring or cached response) for revenue-critical intents — that prevents outages while preserving core functionality."
- Risk matrix (short):
  - Low risk: cosmetic generative features (summaries, creative copy) -> default: aggressive fallback to cheaper model
  - Medium risk: downstream automation with retries -> default: conservative fallback + alerting
  - High risk: legal/finance/medical responses -> default: no model fallback; prefer capacity fallback or human-in-loop

Sample technical appendix (copy/paste snippets):
- Console toggle note: "In Console > Routes > {route} > Edit > Fallbacks: add rule -> targetModel=MODEL-L8-Q; condition=latency_99p>3000ms; action=route"
- Example curl to set routing override: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/override -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"route":"/generate","override_model":"MODEL-L8-Q","ttl_s":900}'
  - note: replace with CLI snippet if desired (TODO: add cli sample).

Playbook checklists (notes to self):
- Add short zone-by-zone cost example table (need real numbers from pricing ops)
- Make a "high-stakes" leaf in the deck for customers who require no fallback — outline alternatives (reserved capacity, private deployment)
- Confirm model variant IDs with model-ops before first SE dry-run

Open questions / research items (for product/ops):
- Can we expose a canned "pilot fallback" template in Console? (product)
- What's the default TTL we should set on routing overrides for pilots? 5m, 15m, 1h? (ops)
- Need per-model inferred quality drop numbers for typical enterprise prompts (applied-ml to supply)

Immediate next actions (owner Aisha):
- Run SE dry-run w/ Marcus + Rae by 2025-03-05. Capture feedback.
- Add CLI examples and replace curl placeholders.
- Get pricing numbers from finance for sample cost delta scenarios and insert into slide 4.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language lightweight; sellers hate 20-slide decks. Aim for 6 slides + single-page one-pager.
- Use concrete customer anecdotes where possible.
- We should track a small prompt set (10–20) per pilot to monitor quality regressions automatically.

End of doc — very rough draft. Expect follow-up iterations after the first SE workshop.
